metadata.title: OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks Lean on 6 Crypto Firms: Will Wall Street Ever Follow?

content.text:
OKX-ICE, an OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) venture, opens tokenized stocks trading Nov. 23 after 56 of 62 targets objected. The six that did not are all crypto-linked, so no non-crypto name among the 62 has joined.
Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, Strategy, Securitize, and BitGo are those six. Better.com and 59 Direxion exchange-traded funds also list, so single-stock access skews toward crypto-linked names. ICE owns the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
Is Wall Street's Silence on Tokenized Stocks Turning Into Consent?
Not so far. Neither Apple nor Nvidia had objected in late October, per BeInCrypto's earlier objection tally. However, both appear among objectors in Fortune's Nov. 5 count.
Objections on the original list rose from 30 in late October to 54 by Nov. 5, then 56 per Bloomberg.
Applied Optoelectronics, a networking equipment maker, filed an objection. It told Fortune that uncertainty over its stock's pricing, liquidity, and volatility remained. It also feared investors would think it sponsored the offering.
Meanwhile, Bloomberg's hosts flagged that 24/7 trading removes the breathing room companies relied on during the 2008 financial crisis.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T162glXDCks
Therefore, issuers may want evidence on pricing and liquidity before backing any venue.
Can Objectors Be Won Over, or Bypassed?
Objections apply venue by venue, so a company that blocks OKX-ICE must object again elsewhere.
In contrast, the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) clears and settles US equity trades. Its tokenization service needs no issuer approval and has 20 participants and 34 securities.
Nadine Chakar, DTCC's managing director and global head of digital assets, tied the refusals to design. Under opt-out rules, silence enrolls a company. She said earlier issuer conversations might have changed the outcome.
Volume caps may also matter. Each token faces a ceiling of 0.25% of the underlying stock's prior-month volume, per BeInCrypto's OKX first-mover analysis. That could ease volatility concerns while limiting the venue's reach.
The test after Nov. 23 is whether any large non-crypto issuer agrees to list. Until one does, tokenization may reach Wall Street through DTCC's infrastructure before stock tokens do.
Read the Original story OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks Lean on 6 Crypto Firms: Will Wall Street Ever Follow? by Darryn Pollock at beincrypto.com
